headline: Dolly Parton's Free Book Program Expands After Her Passing
meta_description: Nearly a month after Dolly Parton's death, her Imagination Library—the free book program she launched in 1995—is growing and continuing her legacy of education.
summary_short: Dolly Parton's beloved Imagination Library is expanding after the country icon's recent passing, keeping her vision of free books alive.
body:
Nearly a month after country icon Dolly Parton passed away, her legacy continues to grow. Beyond her legendary catalog of hit songs and the social issues they highlighted, Parton was perhaps best known for her philanthropy.

In 1988, Parton founded the Dollywood Foundation, establishing her commitment to education and community support. Seven years later, in 1995, she launched the Imagination Library—the program that would become her most famous initiative. The Imagination Library offers free books to children, removing financial barriers to early literacy and learning.

Now, even as the music world mourns her loss, the program she built is experiencing expansion, ensuring that her impact reaches even more young readers in the years ahead.
quick_facts: Dolly Parton founded the Dollywood Foundation in 1988
Program offers free books to children
Expansion announced after Parton's recent death
